mathleague-2004-05-g5-01.title: Compute both sides
mathleague-2004-05-g5-01.body:
The left side is 900. On the right, $100 + 200 + 300 = 600$, so the missing number is $900 - 600 = 300$.

**Answer: (C) 300**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-02.title: Dozens first
mathleague-2004-05-g5-02.body:
Two dozen is $2 \times 12 = 24$. Two fewer than 24 is $24 - 2 = 22$.

**Answer: (D) 22**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-02.title: Careful reading
mathleague-2004-05-g5-02.body:
"2 fewer than 2-dozen" means start at 24 and go down 2, giving 22 (not 2 fewer than one dozen, which would be 10).

**Answer: (D) 22**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-03.title: Compute the left side
mathleague-2004-05-g5-03.body:
$27 \div 3 = 9$, and $9 = 3 \times 3$. So the missing number is 3.

**Answer: (A) 3**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-04.title: Groups of three
mathleague-2004-05-g5-04.body:
For each coin that lands tails up, two land heads up, so the coins come in groups of 3 (1 tail, 2 heads). 9 coins make 3 groups, so there are $3 \times 2 = 6$ heads.

**Answer: (D) 6**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-04.title: Make a list
mathleague-2004-05-g5-04.body:
Tails and heads: 1 and 2 (total 3), 2 and 4 (total 6), 3 and 6 (total 9). So 6 heads.

**Answer: (D) 6**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-05.title: Factor
mathleague-2004-05-g5-05.body:
Each ten minus one leaves 9, so $19 \times 9 = 171$.

**Answer: (C) 171**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-07.title: Count the 5s
mathleague-2004-05-g5-07.body:
50 cm is $50 \div 5 = 10$ growth spurts of 5 cm, each taking 10 days: $10 \times 10 = 100$ days.

**Answer: (D) 100**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-07.title: Rate per day
mathleague-2004-05-g5-07.body:
5 cm in 10 days is $\frac{1}{2}$ cm per day. To grow 50 cm takes $50 \div \frac{1}{2} = 100$ days.

**Answer: (D) 100**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-09.title: Even and divisible by 3
mathleague-2004-05-g5-09.body:
All four are even, so we need the one divisible by 3, i.e., whose digit sum is divisible by 3. Digit sums: 13, 14, 15, 16. Only 366 (digit sum 15) works.

**Answer: (C) 366**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-09.title: Divide
mathleague-2004-05-g5-09.body:
$366 = 6 \times 61$, while 166, 266, 466 leave remainders 4, 2, 4 when divided by 6.

**Answer: (C) 366**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-12.title: Count sides
mathleague-2004-05-g5-12.body:
The perimeter is 4 side-lengths. Dividing 4 side-lengths by 2 side-lengths gives $4 \div 2 = 2$.

**Answer: (B) 2**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-12.title: Try an example
mathleague-2004-05-g5-12.body:
A square with side 5 has perimeter 20; two side-lengths are 10; $20 \div 10 = 2$.

**Answer: (B) 2**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-13.title: Find both ages
mathleague-2004-05-g5-13.body:
4 years ago Tom was 8; 6 years ago he was 6. Their average is $(8 + 6) \div 2 = 7$.

**Answer: (B) 7**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-13.title: Halfway
mathleague-2004-05-g5-13.body:
The average of 4 years ago and 6 years ago is 5 years ago: $12 - 5 = 7$.

**Answer: (B) 7**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-14.title: Go back 12 hours, then 12 minutes
mathleague-2004-05-g5-14.body:
12 hours before noon is midnight. 12 minutes before midnight is 11:48 P.M. (on the previous evening).

**Answer: (C) 11:48 P.M.**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-14.title: Go back 12 minutes first
mathleague-2004-05-g5-14.body:
12 minutes before noon is 11:48 A.M.; another 12 hours earlier is 11:48 P.M.

**Answer: (C) 11:48 P.M.**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-16.title: Add them
mathleague-2004-05-g5-16.body:
The greatest 3-digit number is 999 and the greatest 4-digit number is 9999. Their sum is $999 + 9999 = 10\,998$.

**Answer: (D) 10 998**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-17.title: Bananas per day
mathleague-2004-05-g5-17.body:
A day has 24 hours, so the ape eats $24 \div 4 = 6$ bananas a day, and $5 \times 6 = 30$ bananas in 5 days.

**Answer: (C) 30**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-18.title: Equal sides
mathleague-2004-05-g5-18.body:
All three sides of an equilateral triangle are 6 cm, so the perimeter is $6 + 6 + 6 = 18$ cm.

**Answer: (C) 18**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-19.title: Estimate by months
mathleague-2004-05-g5-19.body:
Months have about 30 days, so the first 6 months take about $6 \times 30 = 180$ days, and day 199 falls in the 7th month, July.

**Answer: (C) July**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-19.title: Count exactly
mathleague-2004-05-g5-19.body:
January to June have 31 + 28 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 = 181 days (182 in a leap year). So day 199 is July 18 (or July 17 in a leap year), in July either way.

**Answer: (C) July**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-20.title: Divide by 72
mathleague-2004-05-g5-20.body:
$72 \times 10 = 720$, so $728 \div 72 = 10$ remainder 8. So 728 is not divisible by 72.

**Answer: (D) 72**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-21.title: Multiply
mathleague-2004-05-g5-21.body:
$1111 \times 1111 = 1\,234\,321$. Its digits are 1, 2, 3, 4; the largest odd one is 3.

**Answer: (B) 3**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-21.title: Add shifted copies
mathleague-2004-05-g5-21.body:
$1111 \times 1111 = 1111000 + 111100 + 11110 + 1111$, written in columns:

$$\begin{array}{r} 1111000 \\ 111100 \\ 11110 \\ 1111 \\ \hline 1234321 \end{array}$$

The largest odd digit is 3.

**Answer: (B) 3**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-22.title: Trial and error
mathleague-2004-05-g5-22.body:
Try each choice as half my number. For A, my number is 6 and twice it is 12; $6 \times 12 = 72$. ✓

**Answer: (A) 3**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-22.title: Simplify
mathleague-2004-05-g5-22.body:
(my number) $\times$ 2 $\times$ (my number) $= 72$, so (my number) $\times$ (my number) $= 36$ and my number is 6. Half of 6 is 3.

**Answer: (A) 3**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-23.title: Start from all 100s
mathleague-2004-05-g5-23.body:
With all 100s her average would be 100. Since 98 is a little less, try four 100s and one 90: $(400 + 90) \div 5 = 98$. ✓ So she got one 90.

**Answer: (A) 1**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-23.title: Total points
mathleague-2004-05-g5-23.body:
An average of 98 on 5 tests means $5 \times 98 = 490$ points, which is 10 less than 500. Each 90 costs 10 points, so there is exactly one 90.

**Answer: (A) 1**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-24.title: Alternating digit sum
mathleague-2004-05-g5-24.body:
Reading the digits 1,2,1,1,2,1,1,2,1,0,0,6 from the right with alternating signs: $6 - 0 + 0 - 1 + 2 - 1 + 1 - 2 + 1 - 1 + 2 - 1 = 6$. So the remainder is 6.

**Answer: (A) 6**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-25.title: Factor out 10
mathleague-2004-05-g5-25.body:
All three are multiples of 10: $60 = 10 \times 6$, $160 = 10 \times 16$, $260 = 10 \times 26$. The g.c.d. of 6, 16, 26 is 2, so the g.c.d. of 60, 160, 260 is $10 \times 2 = 20$.

**Answer: (C) 20**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-25.title: Check the choices
mathleague-2004-05-g5-25.body:
60 does not divide 160. 20 divides all three ($60 = 3 \times 20$, $160 = 8 \times 20$, $260 = 13 \times 20$), and 20 is larger than 5. So 20.

**Answer: (C) 20**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-26.title: Algebra check
mathleague-2004-05-g5-26.body:
If the smallest is $n$, then $5n + 10 = 2005$, so $n = 399$. Same numbers, same digit sum 43.

**Answer: (D) 43**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-27.title: Scale up
mathleague-2004-05-g5-27.body:
2 splashes = 3 splishes. 18 splashes is $9 \times 2$ splashes, so it equals $9 \times 3 = 27$ splishes.

**Answer: (B) 27**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-28.title: Find the range
mathleague-2004-05-g5-28.body:
A number 5 more than a list number is at least $1 + 5 = 6$. A number 5 less than a list number is at most $100 - 5 = 95$. So we need the numbers 6 through 95: there are $95 - 6 + 1 = 90$ of them.

**Answer: (B) 90**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-28.title: Remove the ends
mathleague-2004-05-g5-28.body:
Throw away 1–5 (nothing in the list is 5 less than them) and 96–100 (nothing is 5 more than them). That removes 10 numbers, leaving $100 - 10 = 90$.

**Answer: (B) 90**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-29.title: Use the l.c.m.
mathleague-2004-05-g5-29.body:
A number that is a multiple of both 6 and 9 is a multiple of their l.c.m., 18. The 2-digit multiples of 18 are 18, 36, 54, 72, 90: five numbers.

**Answer: (D) 5**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-29.title: List multiples of 9
mathleague-2004-05-g5-29.body:
Two-digit multiples of 9: 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72, 81, 90, 99. The even ones (so also multiples of 6) are 18, 36, 54, 72, 90: five.

**Answer: (D) 5**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-30.title: Compare term by term
mathleague-2004-05-g5-30.body:
$1 + 3 + \ldots + 99 = (2-1) + (4-1) + \ldots + (100-1)$. There are 50 terms, each 1 less than an even number, so the sum is $2550 - 50 = 2500$.

**Answer: (C) 2500**

mathleague-2004-05-g5-30.title: Pair up
mathleague-2004-05-g5-30.body:
Pair the odd numbers from the ends: $1 + 99 = 100$, $3 + 97 = 100$, ... There are 50 odd numbers, so 25 pairs: $25 \times 100 = 2500$.

**Answer: (C) 2500**
